findings.claim: Quarterly churn rate nearly doubled in Q2 2026 (6.9%) vs. Q1 2026 (3.5%) — 92 customers lost, $838K ARR walked.
findings.evidence: Exposure-adjusted: at-risk = customers signed up on/before quarter start and not already churned. Churn rate column = churned_in_quarter / at_risk.

findings.claim: The spike is concentrated in the Pro tier: Q2-26 Pro-tier churn rate 10.6% vs. 5.3% Starter and 3.9% Enterprise — 2x the rate of any other tier.
findings.evidence: Q2-26 at-risk: Pro=463, Starter=655, Ent=206. Churned: Pro=49, Starter=35, Ent=8.
findings.hypothesis_tested: H2 (partial: not lowest tier — it's middle tier)

findings.claim: Within Pro tier, Retail (21.6%) and Manufacturing (14.1%) are 3-6x the Q2-26 churn rate of other Pro industries (3.8%-8.0%) — two industries drive the Pro spike.
findings.evidence: Pro x industry pivot, Q2-26. Pro-Retail churned 21/97, Pro-Mfg 11/78, Pro-Finance 8/100, Pro-Healthcare 4/105, Pro-SaaS 5/83.
findings.hypothesis_tested: H3 (confirmed but industry is conditional on tier)

findings.claim: Pro-Retail & Pro-Manufacturing alone account for 64% of the *jump* in churn count Q1→Q2 2026 (+28 of +44 net new churns) and 50% of the jump in churned ARR ($235K of $470K).
findings.evidence: Q1-26 Pro-Retail+Mfg churn=4, Q2-26=32 (+28). Total Q1-26=48, Q2-26=92 (+44). ARR delta: Pro-Retail+Mfg $235K of $470K total.

validation.method: direct Q1-26 vs Q2-26 count subtraction per subset

findings.claim: The Pro-Retail/Mfg spike is *segment-and-time-specific*, not a cohort renewal effect: both the 2025Q1, Q2, and Q3 signup cohorts within Pro-Retail all show 18-27% Q2-26 churn — ruling out the 'cohorts are hitting their renewal cliff' explanation.
findings.evidence: Pro-Retail Q2-26 by signup cohort: 2025Q1 18.4%, 2025Q2 20.7%, 2025Q3 26.7% — all similar.

findings.claim: Pro-Retail churn rate was 1.0% in Q1 2026 and jumped to 21.6% in Q2 2026 (21x). This is a structural break, not a drift — the trigger occurred within the quarter.
If Q2-26 rates persist for 4 quarters, Pro-Retail + Pro-Mfg alone lose ~$654K ARR; if rates revert to Q1-26 baseline, loss is ~$105K. Intervention opportunity: ~$549K ARR preservation.
findings.evidence: Active Pro-Retail=76, Pro-Mfg=67. Applied geometric decay at Q2-26 rates (21.6% / 14.1%) vs Q1-26 rates (1.0% / 3.7%) over 4 quarters, multiplied by $8.4K ARR/customer.
findings.caveat: Geometric decay is a simple model; actual trajectory depends on whether Q2-26 rate is a one-time event or new baseline.

findings.claim: Starter tier churn rate drifted up modestly (from 3.5% Q1-26 to 5.3% Q2-26) — meaningful but not a crisis. ~$42K ARR in Q2-26 vs. $412K from Pro.

metadata.headline: The Q2-2026 churn spike is not broad — two segments (Pro-Retail and Pro-Manufacturing) drove 64% of the new churn, and a targeted 90-day intervention can save roughly $0.5M ARR over the next year.

recommendations.action: 90-day Pro-Retail save program: dedicated CSM, executive sponsor calls to all 76 active Pro-Retail accounts, structured save template
2-week root-cause sprint: 25 customer interviews + product/pricing/GTM timeline audit
recommendations.owner: Head of Product + Head of Sales (joint)
recommendations.success_metric: 2-page memo naming the Q2 trigger by May 2

recommendations.action: Put Pro-Manufacturing on weekly watch; activate save play if Q3-26 rate > 10%

caveats: Dataset covers only customers signed up 2025Q1–Q3 (<=18 months tenure). Customers acquired earlier are not observable here; conclusions should not be extrapolated to legacy tenure cohorts without additional data.
The data identifies where the spike occurred (Pro-Retail and Pro-Manufacturing in Q2-26). It does NOT identify why — that requires qualitative discovery (R2).
ARR savings projection ($549K) assumes geometric decay; sensitivity range is $105K–$654K depending on whether Q2-26 is a new baseline or a one-time event.
